The Collapse in South African Cricket part 2

By: Julian Sun | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Is the ongoing turmoil engulfing Cricket South Africa posing an existential threat to the game?

Unique Selling Point:
In January we ran a story about the crisis facing cricket. 8 months later and the game seems in even worse shape than then with a spate of high-profile resignations and the failure by CSA to release a much anticipated forensic audit into its affairs. We investigate why cricket remains such a mess to reveal those responsible.

Summary:
There have been accusations made that CSA is being run by a powerful cabal within the board. We will reveal if this is true

We investigate allegations made against these 3 senior administrators

1. Welsh Gwaza - Company secretary who is said to be the real power behind the throne. We have information that findings have been made against him in the forensic audit and that he has been at the forefront of blocking its release.

2. Eugenia Kula-Ameyaw a newly appointed Independent Director at CSA. She heads CSA's Social Justice and Renewal Project that has board approval and a R10 million budget. However she is accused of forcing through an advert in the Sunday Times for an amount of R521000 that did not have board or CEO approval

Press Release:


In January it seemed like the administration of Cricket South Africa had turned a corner and begun the long road towards rehabilitation. But eight months later, the gentleman’s game is in a freefall. Inside the boardrooms of the game's governing body, the gloves are off as more explosive revelations lead to high-profile resignations. Now the Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture has issued CSA with a notice that government intends to intervene in the crumbling sports. Carte Blanche examines whether cricket in South Africa can be saved.
Producer: Julian Sun | Presenter: Claire Mawisa

Script:


V/O: Cricket is a national sport of South Africa. Millions of kids around the country dream of one day playing for the Proteas against the best in the world. But what happens when that dream is threatened?

Accusations of maladministration within Cricket South Africa could lead to government intervention and a ban from world cricket

LINK: I’m standing outside the headquarters of CSA here in a leafy suburb of Johannesburg. But the tranquil surroundings bely an organization in a crisis that threatens the very future of the game.

V/O: Last November former CEO Thabang Moroe ignited a firestorm when he removed the accreditation of journalists. This resulted in a media outcry and Standard Bank withdrawing their sponsorship (citing reputational harm).

Moroe was suspended and Jacques Faul installed as acting CEO.

A profitable season against England & Australia followed.

But since then 2020 has been disastrous.

The pandemic has forced the Proteas from the playing field, while continued boardroom turmoil resulted in the resignation of president Chris Nenzani and Jacques Faul in August. Neil Manthorp is a respected cricket journalist

Neil gives summary

V/O: Cricket writer Luke Alfred explains what’s gone wrong

Jacques Faul was always under the belief that the board never really wanted him.

He tried to mend things, he wanted to keep momentum on board, there was a possibility of getting Standard Bank back because cricket needs money from sponsors and broadcast rights. there were people behind the scenes who did not buy into the reform initiative



V/O: In May CSA announced the appointment of 3 new independent board members One of them was Dr Eugenia Kula-Ameyaw. Describing herself as “a social entrepreneur and strategist with public & private corporate experience”, this is her first foray into sports administration

EUGENIA: I joined in May, literally conducted a month later in June, and by July there was an outbreak of Black Lives Matter. And I happened to maybe for my sins or passion to chair the transformation committee

V/O: She spearheads the “Cricket for Social Justice and Nation Building” initiative in response to the Black Lives Matter protest.

To promote the project, CSA placed an advert in the Sunday Times at a cost of R521000. It led to the resignation of Jacques Faul

Luke Alfred & Neil tell why Jacques resigned

V/O: Carte Blanche has seen internal emails that detail how CSA CFO Pholetsi Moseki was asked to approve the cost of the advert.

He expresses his discomfort

He later writes that Dr Eugenia accused him of trying to sabotage this “board-approved initiative” and instructed him to approve the payment”.

Dr Eugenia defends herself

V/O: CSA are investigating whether the proper procedures were followed says board member John Mogodi

John comments about Eugenia having a hearing to defend herself.

V/O: The Pandora’s box of cricket is the Fundudzi Forensic Audit, commissioned by the Members Council of CSA to investigate the tenure of former CEO Thabang Moroe.

Neil talks about:
1. Why CSA won’t release the report
2. Damning findings are made against Thabang Moroe

V/O: CSA used the report to dismiss Moroe. Among the findings is that he breached the company’s act 12 times.

He did not respond to our request for an interview

The report was completed in July but on legal advice, CSA have not made the full report public.

John Mogodi explains why the report has not been made public



V/O: The summary also makes findings against others - including company secretary Welsh Gwaza (who plays a very influential role at CSA).

Luke explains the role of company secretary:

12:38 The people who are running CSA at the moment are nominally Kugandrie Govender as acting CEO and Beresford Williams as acting President but Welsh Gwaza is very influential as company secretary.

Neil explains that when Jacques & Chris resigned their emails were forwarded to Welsh

V/O: In an excerpt from the audit seen by Carte Blanche the report finds that Mr Gwaza failed to fulfil his fiduciary obligation, with regard to an international broadcast rights agreement for the Mzansi Super League.

It says that he failed to inform the board that due diligence was not done and a bank guarantee was not obtained - placing CSA at huge risk.

We requested an interview with Mr Gwaza through CSA.

Board Member John Mogodi was made available to comment on his behalf

John Mogodi’s right of reply on behalf of Welsh
V/O: The controversy surrounding the audit resulted in CSA postponing its AGM. This led to SASCOC calling on the board to step aside to allow a task team to probe CSA’s affairs. When talks broke down, the matter was referred to the Minister of Sports and Recreation Nathi Mthethwa.

Angered by the board, the minister wrote to the ICC of his intention to intervene into the affairs of cricket

This could lead to the Proteas being suspended from international cricket, with catastrophic consequences.

He has given CSA until Tuesday to explain why he shouldn’t take such a drastic step


Neil talks about how the minister is forcing the icc’s hand

We get John’s response


Claire suggests the board steps aside, John replies

V/O: Then on Friday it was reported that CSA’s Members Council had asked the entire board to step down.

Later that night CSA released a statement saying no resignations had taken place. The question remains: will they do so?

Neil’s last comment about how for the first time, he fears for the future of professional cricket in SA
